newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippines sees little hope of infotech pact.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees little hope of infotech pact.

text.p: The Philippines predicted on Tuesday that there was little chance of a concrete agreement to eliminate tariffs on information technology being reached at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting here.

"I doubt if there will be concete agreements coming out this week," Philippine Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista told reporters at a news conference when asked about the prospects for an agreement to lower tariff barriers on information technology substantially by the year 2000.
"It's too fast for us," he said.
"I think it will be more in a general manner of information," he said, refering to the wording likely to be adopted on infotech by 128 countries attending the week-long meeting, which ends on Friday.
It is the first ministerial conference of the two-year-old WTO, which sets international trade rules.
Washington has been pressing for a deal on both infotech and telecommunications to pry open computer and phone markets around the world worth billions of dollars.
Countries including Malaysia and Indonesia have baulked, saying there should be flexibility for fledgling computer industries.

Bautista dismissed demands by the United States and France to include labour standards in the WTO because such a measure would just be used by developed nations as a protectionist measure to keep out products from poorer nations.
"The impact of this if we agree to this naive position is we will probably lose jobs. When their constituents complain, they will close the door to our products," he said.
